0.0.n: Sets the occasion for the award announcement.

0.2.n: The country name modifies 音楽文化 through の.

0.3.n: Links Japan to its music culture.

0.4.n: Combines with 文化 to describe a musical culture.

0.5.n: Together with 音楽, forms the thing whose development is being discussed.

0.6.n: Links music culture to its development.

0.7.n: Names the first of two things she helped advance.

0.8.n: Joins the development of music culture and the building of international relations.

0.10.n: Uses な before a noun to describe relations as favorable.

0.11.n: Connects 良好 to the noun phrase 日豪関係.

0.12.n: An abbreviation for 日本 in 日豪, meaning Japan and Australia.

0.13.n: An abbreviation for 豪州, a Japanese name for Australia.

0.14.n: 日豪関係 refers to ties between Japan and Australia.

0.15.n: Links the international relations to their establishment.

0.16.n: Used figuratively for establishing relationships, not constructing a physical structure.

0.17.n: Marks what she contributed to, covering both development and relationship-building.

0.18.n: 貢献した is the plain past form of 貢献する.

0.19.n: After a statement, として presents the recognized reason for the award.

1.0.n: This segment combines 旭日 and 小 within the award name 旭日小綬章; it is not a standalone word.

1.1.n: Part of 小綬章 within the award name, whose official English grade is Gold Rays with Rosette.

1.2.n: Ends the award name; 章 here refers to an honor or medal.

1.4.n: The noun 受章 ends this news-style sentence, with しました left unstated.

2.0.n: Refers to the present moment in the expression これまで.

2.1.n: Combined with これ, sets the time span ending now.

2.3.n: A borrowed word; Japanese does not mark it as singular or plural here.

2.4.n: Shows concerts are examples, not the complete list.

2.5.n: Marks concerts and similar events as the occasions for her visits.

2.6.n: 回 counts how many times an event happens.

2.7.n: Includes the stated number, so 10回以上 includes exactly ten visits.

2.8.n: 来日する becomes polite 来日しています, describing accumulated visits up to now rather than an ongoing arrival.

2.9.n: Gently links background information to the next statement rather than expressing a strong contrast.

3.0.n: 年 follows the number to mark a calendar year.

3.2.n: Part of 東日本大震災, the name of the 2011 earthquake disaster.

3.3.n: Combines with 東日本 to name the Great East Japan Earthquake disaster.

3.4.n: Links the named disaster to the area affected by it.

3.5.n: Refers to a place damaged by the earthquake disaster.

3.6.n: Marks where the performance took place.

3.7.n: Plain past form of 行う, modifying the performance that follows; here it is not 行く, to go.

3.8.n: Directly combines with 公演 to describe the performance.

3.9.n: Refers to a public artistic show, here a musical event.

3.10.n: Marks the special performance as what she looked back on.

3.11.n: Points forward to the speaker’s words quoted next.

3.12.n: Polite past form of 振り返る, used figuratively for recalling a past experience.

0.lit: This time, on grounds of having contributed to Japanese music culture’s development and building good Japan–Australia relations,
0.tip: 貢献したとして gives the recognized reason for the award announced in the next line.

1.lit: Received the Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Rosette.
1.tip: News reports can end with a noun like 受章 instead of the full polite verb 受章しました.

2.lit: Up to now, for concerts and such, she has visited Japan ten times or more, and,
2.tip: 以上 includes the number before it: 10回以上 means at least ten times.

3.lit: She thus recalled the special performance held in 2015 in the Great East Japan Earthquake’s disaster-hit area.
3.tip: 行った comes before 特別公演 to describe which performance she recalled.
